identity_metric: DINOv2-small CLS cosine on DECODED pixels (whole-image; torchvision-free manual ImageNet preprocess)
ref_prompt: a portrait of a woman with distinctive curly red hair and green eyes, plain grey background
reading: A real appearance-identity metric (DINOv2 on decoded pixels) confirms the character-pin. Identity curve: same sharp k~4 crossover (sim_to_ref -0.02 at k1 -> 0.70 at k3 -> 0.99 at k4). PERSISTENCE at k=3 across four unrelated scenes: pinned outputs match the reference at 0.79 mean (vs baselines ~0, and vs the scene's inherent ~0.02) AND match EACH OTHER at 0.72 pairwise (vs 0.14 for un-pinned baselines) -> the same character persists across many images. HONEST CAVEAT: whole-latent replacement transfers identity by importing the reference COMPOSITION (a portrait), so the scene degrades to a backdrop (sim_to_scene only 0.20 at k3). Placing the pinned character INTO the scene action (not as a portrait) needs sub-latent / regional / attention-level injection, not whole-latent replacement. Metric is whole-image DINOv2, not a face-cropped ArcFace (no face model available offline).
